lines.speaker: ansel
lines.text: Ansel. Commons assembly. We run this town by argument — nine of us, a lamp, and whoever else turns up. It is slower than an algorithm and every bit of it is ours.

lines.speaker: ansel
lines.text: The assembly voted to keep the blades on the memorial wall rather than melt them down for the metal, which we badly need. Forty minutes of argument about it. Somebody has to remember that people fought for this, and a thing you can put your hand on remembers better than a thing you write down.

lines.speaker: ansel
lines.text: You sound like somebody who has made their peace with the Steward. Some of us have, and I do not think less of them for it: it feeds them, it houses them, it has never once been cruel. The rest of us keep the assembly meeting anyway — not because it is better, but because it is a habit rather than a service.

lines.speaker: ansel
lines.text: Practical matter, since you are travelling. Every era has its own money and none of it travels. Relics are the exception: old things, made things, anything with a hand in it. Any shop in any century will take one. Carry five at most — they are heavy and they attract questions.
